Thanks Jonathan — this is perfect context. Attaching a draft runbook that outlines our standard connector onboarding flow and the artifacts we accept (redwood-connector-runbook-draft.md). High-level answers below, we can walk through details on the call: 

- Evidence escrow: Yes, we support third-party artifact escrow via our secure artifact store. There are two modes: short-term (90–180 days) for operational transfers, and long-term escrow (1–5 years) via an encrypted S3 bucket with KMS-managed keys. Long-term escrow requires a signed addendum (we'll surface contract language).
- Transport: Preferred is HTTPS with mutual TLS for automated pushes, falling back to SFTP for legacy vendors. We can also accept signed bundles via secure drop with checksum verification.
- Redaction guidance: We redact PII at the field level, prefer tokenized identifiers in logs, and ask for a redaction map in the artifact metadata. Our runbook includes an example mapping.

Pre-kickoff checklist (please confirm these items before 10/5):
- AuditWorks to confirm artifact types and canonical filenames (you sent a start, thanks)
- Confirm retention policy per artifact type (which need long-term escrow)
- Provide primary technical contact for connector implementation and a secondary for ops (Elena can be one if she prefers)
- Any legal/SLA constraints around artifact access (e.g., restricted access windows)

Proposed agenda for 10/5 (30 mins): scope & artifact mapping (10m), transport & auth (mTLS vs SFTP) (10m), escrow and retention (5m), next steps & timeline (5m).

I'll send the Confluence runbook link and attach the draft. Ben — looping you in to track procurement / MSA milestones. Neha — can you confirm our redaction/retention defaults on the call?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Security Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-connector-runbook-draft.md (text, 24KB)
